rappel_detail.anchor: anchor on a small ledge, east side just below the summit
rappel_detail.station: A small ledge on the east side, slightly below the summit, reached by downclimbing the final scramble.
rappel_detail.notes: Rappel 1 of 4, down the steepest upper wall to the shoulder.
hazards: Rockfall-prone: the next rappeller should move off to the side at the bottom, not straight down, since others may be rappelling above.

rappel_detail.anchor: belay/anchor stance at the bottom of the shoulder
rappel_detail.notes: Rappel 2 of 4, a full single 60 m rope doubled, to the belay station at the top of the second climbing pitch.
hazards: The buttress rock is loose enough that downclimbing this section is not recommended.

rappel_detail.anchor: belay station at the top of pitch 2 (fixed natural slings)
rappel_detail.station: The belay station at the top of the second climbing pitch, a tree at the top of the drop overlooking the V-notch.
rappel_detail.notes: Rappel 3 of 4: on a single rope, the first half of the overhanging drop, to an intermediate stance. With two ropes, this and the next are one double-rope rappel.
hazards: The rappel is overhanging. Knot the rope ends.

rappel_detail.anchor: intermediate anchor (natural slings or cord; carry cord to rebuild)
rappel_detail.station: Intermediate stance partway down the overhanging section.
rappel_detail.notes: Rappel 4 of 4, to just below the north side of Gunsight Notch.
hazards: Anchors here have been found needing extra cord or a rebuild.

set.rappels: 4 rappels on a single 60 m rope, or three with two ropes; one lower rappel is overhanging
set.rappel_count_note: Counted for one 60 m rope: a rappel from a ledge just below the summit, a single-rope rappel from the bottom of the shoulder to the top of pitch 2, then the overhanging drop to below Gunsight Notch in two rappels. With two ropes, that last drop is one double-rope rappel, so three in all. Anchors are natural slings and cord; parties report adding cord to one and rebuilding another.
set.descent: Not a simple reverse of the ascent: most parties make four rappels on a single 60 m rope (three with two ropes) back down to Gunsight Notch, including one overhanging double-rope rappel just below/north of the notch, then re-descend the glacier/snowfield and Mixup Arm to Cascade Pass. A 60m rope is recommended for the standard rappel line — the older single-30m-rope beta undersells what's needed. Move away from the fall line immediately after rappelling; rockfall knocked loose by the party above or below is a recognized hazard on this descent.
set.descent_text: Descend by reversing the final scramble pitches/downclimbing back to the top of the technical face (the uppermost section is a downclimb/scramble to the top of the East Face), then begin a rappel sequence rather than trying to downclimb the buttress itself — the rock is loose enough that down-climbing the route is not recommended. From a small ledge/anchor on the east side just below the summit, a 50 m rappel gets you down the steepest upper wall (rockfall-prone — the next rappeller should move off to the side immediately, not straight down, to avoid anyone above). Below that, from the bottom of the shoulder, one rappel on a single 60 m rope reaches the belay station at the top of the second climbing pitch. From there the line drops over an overhanging section to just below the north side of Gunsight Notch: one double-rope rappel with two ropes, or two rappels on a single 60 m rope. That is four rappels on one 60 m rope, which is what parties report, or three with two ropes. Anchors are fixed natural slings and cord rather than bolts, and parties regularly add cord or rebuild one, so carry some. Move off the fall line as soon as you are down each rappel; rockfall knocked loose by the party above is a recognized hazard here. Below the notch, re-descend the glacier and snowfield and Mixup Arm to Cascade Pass.
